title: feat(sleep): opt-in suspend battery floor for laptops without hibernation
head: bbcb542a3078
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Online USB charger variants can be treated as battery power, causing a plugged-in laptop to power off
leads.consequence: At expiry, an online USB_DCP or USB_CDP supply (both emitted by Linux v7.2 charger drivers) is ignored by omarchy-power-present. Other kernel-defined types, including USB_PD, USB_C, USB_ACA, USB_PD_DRP, BrickID and Wireless, are likewise ignored when exposed as the supply's type. If no separate online Mains or plain USB supply exists, the new act phase consequently takes the battery branch and issues systemctl poweroff instead of suspend even while externally powered. The request's result is hidden. These are kernel-defined type strings, not hypothetical spellings.
leads.triage: dropped; omarchy-power-present charger types: pre-existing shared helper, not changed by PR; impact on AC is a power-off instead of re-suspend. Outside follow-up scope.

leads.summary: Physically connected but disabled displays cancel the floor even when logind will suspend the closed lid
leads.consequence: The monitor helper calls a connected HDMI/DP port docked without checking its enabled attribute. systemd v262 explicitly excludes enabled=disabled from its external-display count, and thus handles this as an undocked lid. An early wake with the lid shut in this configuration disables the RTC and deletes the deadline; logind may re-suspend the closed lid, this time without an alarm or battery floor, so the machine can drain to zero. At expiry act also stands down on the false dock signal.
leads.triage: dropped; external-monitors counts disabled connectors: pre-existing helper premise; edge case. Not verified.

leads.summary: The battery gate excludes valid batteries with no present field or a non-BAT name
leads.consequence: The kernel ABI explicitly says an absent present file means the battery is present, but this helper requires a readable present=1; it also scans only BAT* even though the kernel registers Battery devices such as qcom-battmgr-bat and max170xx_battery. In either case setup says No battery detected and returns success without installing; an already-installed hook silently exits before arming. --force cannot override the battery gate. Restricting this finding to batteries that actually expose these kernel-supported shapes avoids implying every laptop is affected.
leads.triage: dropped; omarchy-battery-present naming/present file: pre-existing helper, affects setup gate already reviewed in R1; out of follow-up scope.

leads.summary: A lid exposed through evdev/logind but not the ACPI procfs lid path leaves the new floor inert
leads.consequence: omarchy-hw-laptop-closed checks only /proc/acpi/button/lid/*/state. Linux ACPI button creates this path only for an ACPI lid device, while systemd logind can know the lid is closed via SW_LID input events without any such ACPI path. If the battery gate succeeds on such a machine, setup reports success but every pre suspend treats the closed lid as open and never arms a floor; on early wake it can clear a deadline. Open PR #7951 explicitly fixes this helper, and is a related dependency, not a textual conflict with this PR.
leads.triage: dropped; omarchy-hw-laptop-closed relies on /proc/acpi lid: pre-existing helper; related open PR #7951. Out of scope.

leads.summary: rtcwake -m no can succeed with a wake-disabled RTC and leave the machine without any self-wake
leads.consequence: util-linux v2.42.4 checks whether the selected RTC has power/wakeup enabled when it itself suspends, but intentionally skips that check for -m no. Linux rtc-cmos disables its RTC alarm interrupt during suspend when device_may_wakeup is false. Thus on a machine with RTC wake disabled, -m no -s 1200 can set the RTC alarm and return success while that alarm cannot wake the suspended machine. The hook sees no error, writes a deadline and continues into unbounded battery drain. This is a separate failure mode from H6's nonzero rtcwake result; setup offers no eligibility warning.
leads.triage: dropped; rtc-cmos masking when wake disabled: hardware-dependent, unverified.

leads.summary: Docks are not checked at pre, despite the advertised undocked-only countdown
leads.consequence: A deliberate manual suspend with a closed lid and connected external monitor writes the deadline and arms a 20-minute RTC alarm. The dock is first checked on post, after this wake. Post then disables the alarm and exits; logind's default docked lid action is ignore, so a manually suspended clamshell can remain awake after 20 minutes. The manual says only an undocked suspend starts the countdown, and the setup confirmation says undocked. The existing functional test checks dock only during act, not at pre.
leads.triage: corroborates; Same as Opus N3 (docked clamshell arms). Published.

leads.summary: Removing the floor does not cancel its already-armed RTC alarm
leads.consequence: Remove deletes the hook and runtime directory but never issues rtcwake -m disable. If called during a countdown on an awake machine, the RTC alarm remains set and may wake a subsequent sleep about 20 minutes after the earlier suspend; the removed hook cannot process that wake. The script reports removed (and also ignores a failed sudo rm -rf of the runtime directory). An alarm's ability to wake soft-off is hardware-dependent, so that is not asserted.
leads.triage: corroborates; Same as Opus M2 (remove does not disarm pending alarm). Local only, hardware-dependent.

leads.summary: A failed rtcwake leaves a live deadline but no guaranteed wakeup, silently defeating the floor
leads.consequence: The hook writes its deadline before asking rtcwake to arm, suppresses rtcwake stderr and exit with || true, and retains that deadline on failure. A lid-shut suspend with an unavailable, unwakeable or failing RTC has no self-wake; in the absence of another wake it continues draining indefinitely despite the setup command reporting success. The same suppression on an early re-arm can strand the existing countdown. A diagnostic or eligibility check can leave suspend unblocked without falsely treating an unsuccessful alarm as protection.
leads.triage: dropped; Failed rtcwake leaves deadline without wake: low value; errors deliberately suppressed so suspend is never blocked.

leads.summary: The hook overwrites and later disables another owner's RTC wake alarm
leads.consequence: rtcwake -m no sets the RTC alarm without reading or preserving a preexisting alarm. rtcwake -m disable clears that same alarm even if another system component changed it while this floor was active. On opt-in machines this can cancel a user's scheduled RTC wake or replace it with the 20-minute wake, and post can disarm an unrelated alarm. The kernel RTC interface has one aie_timer for RTC_WKALM_SET, while separate alarmtimer wake timers use the RTC timer queue and are not asserted to be overwritten.
leads.triage: dropped; RTC alarm ownership conflicts: speculative, low value.

leads.summary: A preexisting unit with the fixed omarchy-battery-floor.service name makes expiry a silent no-op
leads.consequence: systemd-run --unit=omarchy-battery-floor resolves to omarchy-battery-floor.service. systemd v262 refuses StartTransientUnit when that name already has a loaded unit or fragment. The hook has already consumed the deadline and disabled its RTC alarm, then discards systemd-run stderr and error; it cannot retry or power off on later wakes, so a custom unit with that name defeats the feature. This is conditional on an existing unit, not a claim that Omarchy currently ships one.
leads.triage: dropped; Fixed unit name collision: Opus assessed negligible (--collect, ~5 s lifetime).

leads.summary: A corrected system clock can move the 20-minute floor earlier or later than real elapsed time
leads.consequence: Pre writes a deadline from date +%s (wall clock), but RTC wake is programmed for elapsed seconds. If the clock is corrected backward on resume, post treats a full 20-minute RTC wake as early and re-arms a longer timeout; if corrected forward, an earlier unrelated wake can trigger the deferred power decision before 20 minutes. The code does not record elapsed time using CLOCK_BOOTTIME or otherwise reconcile wall-clock steps. A fixture with time 1000 at pre and 500 at post retained deadline 2200 and re-armed for 1700 seconds, demonstrating the boundary arithmetic, not a real-world NTP frequency claim.
leads.triage: dropped; Wall-clock corrections vs relative RTC alarm: edge case, not verified.

leads.summary: Related PR #12125 can leave this floor installed alongside a new default 20-minute hibernation policy
leads.consequence: If this floor is installed first, then #12125's hibernation setup succeeds, neither feature removes the floor. On battery lid close, logind requests suspend-then-hibernate with HibernateDelaySec=20min and this hook independently arms an RTC alarm with a 20-minute deadline. systemd processes post suspend before deciding whether to hibernate; a floor deadline reached then launches an act unit while the hibernation operation may still be in progress. Whether the deferred poweroff races a hibernate or merely gets refused depends on ordering and hardware wake time; no deterministic outcome is claimed. Settle by running the combined stack through isolated simulated s2h orchestration or on assigned hardware.
leads.triage: dropped; Interaction with open PR #12125: explicitly a hypothesis; no conflict asserted.

leads.summary: Manual promises poweroff at expiry even though on AC the hook suspends again
leads.consequence: The manual says 'When it expires, the machine powers off cleanly' without the battery qualifier. The current hook branches on external power: when charging with lid down, it requests suspend and exits. In the same paragraph the feature is presented as applying only on battery, while pre actually arms on AC too. Readers cannot use the documented consequence to decide whether opt-in is appropriate.
leads.triage: published; Verified manual/36-system-sleep.md:23 vs battery-floor:45-47; published as Documentation note.

leads.summary: Functional test accepts a deferred unit that never calls the act phase
leads.consequence: The systemd-run stub only logs its arguments, and the expiry assertion checks for the substring systemd-run rather than that it receives the hook and act. A plausible broken hook replacing "$0" act with /bin/true still passes every battery-floor assertion even though the deferred service cannot power off or resuspend. Add an argument assertion for the executable and act (and a start-failure scenario). This is a test-fidelity issue below the runtime findings.
leads.triage: corroborates; Opus mutation run also missed wrong systemd-run arguments; not separately published.

leads.summary: The privileged-hook security fixture excludes the newly added battery-floor setup command
leads.consequence: The existing root-owned, executable, atomically published hook checks enumerate only omarchy-hibernation-setup and omarchy-toggle-hybrid-gpu. The new omarchy-battery-floor-setup copies the same install_root_file pattern but is absent from that list; its own test only checks literal source/destination strings and syntax. A regression replacing -o root with a non-root owner or publishing before the mode is set would leave a privileged system-sleep hook unsecured while its dedicated test passes. Add bin/omarchy-battery-floor-setup to the line-136 fixture loop and verify its destination/mode as done at lines 148-169.
leads.triage: local_only; Verified unowned-system-paths-test.sh:136 omits battery-floor-setup; removed from public text after editorial check 3c15aaaa (no demonstrated benefit).

limits: No actual suspend, RTC hardware, systemd manager, or logind action was invoked. RTC wake on particular firmware and race ordering of independent timerfd/RTC wake requests remain unproven.

The CLI suite passed on the pinned head once (plan-full run 20260927T183724Z-1fa107fd) but failed twice on the synthetic current-base merge at an unrelated VS Code theme symlink assertion (plan-merged runs 20260927T184137Z onward). The battery-floor and bin-style suites passed on both; do not infer a PR-caused CLI failure from those runs.

A fixed unit-name collision (H8) is conditional on a custom unit, not established as present in the shipped package. H13 is explicitly hypothetical regarding the outcome of two separate 20-minute wake policies; no hardware timing observation was made.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12427#issuecomment-5830625585) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12427#issuecomment-5846736674), checked at `bbcb542a`.

**Verified:** the restructure fixes the main mechanism of the earlier findings. Three gaps remain, one of them in the new deadline logic.

| Earlier finding | At `bbcb542a` |
|---|---|
| `poweroff`/`suspend` refused inside the post hook | **Mostly resolved.** The post hook no longer calls `systemctl`. The decision runs in a transient `systemd-run` unit. It is not ordered after the suspend job yet (see below). |
| Early wakes treated like the alarm | **Mostly resolved.** An early wake no longer acts. A lid-open or docked early wake disarms the alarm and clears the deadline, and expiry disarms it. The countdown still restarts on each early lid-shut wake (see below). |
| Self-wake after a lid-open or docked suspend stays awake | **Lid-open case resolved.** The docked clamshell case remains (see below). |
| Synchronous `sleep 5` delays every resume | **Resolved.** No hook sleeps. The only wait is in the `act` unit, which systemd-sleep does not wait for, so it no longer delays the thaw. |
| Documentation and wording notes | **Resolved** in the hook comment, manual, setup messages, `docs/file-layout.md` and `omarchy-battery-floor-remove`. The PR description still describes the earlier design, the suspend-then-hibernate delay and 24/24. |

### The countdown restarts on every early lid-shut wake

With the lid shut, `pre` always writes a fresh deadline and arms the full 1200 s (`battery-floor:71-72`), even when an unexpired deadline exists. After an early wake with the lid still shut, logind re-suspends once its 30 s lid holdoff ends (systemd v262 defaults; Omarchy does not override `HandleLidSwitch`). That suspend runs `pre` again, which overwrites the remaining-time re-arm from `post` (`:92`).

Stubbed multi-phase run of the hook (`T0` = first suspend, synthetic clock):

```text
pre         t=T0       deadline=T0+1200   rtcwake -m no -s 1200
post early  t=T0+600   deadline=T0+1200   rtcwake -m no -s 600
pre again   t=T0+630   deadline=T0+1830   rtcwake -m no -s 1200   <- countdown restarted
post        t=T0+1260  deadline=T0+1830   rtcwake -m no -s 570    (no act at the original deadline)
```

With an early wake every 15 minutes, the deadline keeps moving and the floor never fires.

**Impact:** Each early lid-shut wake (a charger event or wake-on-USB, as the hook comment lists) postpones the floor by about 20 minutes, and repeated early wakes prevent it. This is the second half of the earlier early-wake finding, still present. The manual ("tracked across early wakes", "just re-arms the remaining time") and the setup message ("even on early wakes") describe behavior the code does not have.

**Suggested change:** Let `pre` continue an unexpired deadline (arm `deadline - now`) instead of starting over. To avoid shortening the grace after someone actually used the machine (no hook runs when the lid opens while awake), carry the deadline only when the suspend closely follows an early wake, for example by recording the early-wake time in `post`.

### The `act` unit is not ordered after the suspend job

`systemd-run` without `--no-block` waits only for the start job of the transient service, which completes at fork. So `act` starts while the post hook is still running, inside the suspend job. It relies on its 5 s wait (`:35`) for the rest of the job to finish:

```text
post hook -> systemd-run ... act     (unit starts now)
  act: sleep 5
other post hooks finish (run in parallel; systemd-sleep waits for all)
thaw user.slice -> suspend job completes -> logind clears the pending action
  act: systemctl poweroff            (accepted only if the job finished within ~5 s)
```

Until the job completes, logind refuses with "Action … already in progress" (`method_do_shutdown_or_sleep()` and `match_job_removed()` in `src/login/logind-dbus.c`). For example, the repository's `force-igpu` hook, installed when `omarchy toggle hybrid-gpu` selects Integrated mode on a supergfxctl laptop, sleeps 4 s in its post branch and then runs two GPU mode switches (`force-igpu:52-64`). Whether that exceeds the window is hardware-dependent and was not measured.

**Impact:** When the call is refused, `|| true` hides it. The deadline is already consumed (`battery-floor:106`) and the alarm disabled, so logind re-suspends the shut lid, `pre` arms a fresh 20 minutes, and the original wake-and-resuspend cycle returns on those machines. The earlier review's first suggestion (a `systemd-run --on-active=…` unit) makes the same timing assumption. Only its `After=suspend.target` option orders the action after the job.

**Suggested change** (from source, untested): `systemd-run --no-block --property=After=suspend.target … "$0" act`. `--no-block` is needed: without it, `systemd-run` waits for a start job that waits for the suspend job, which waits for this hook. Alternatively, have `act` retry until logind accepts. On hardware, the check is whether logind's `Operation 'suspend' finished.` appears before `poweroff requested … (unit omarchy-battery-floor.service)`. Per source, the transient unit starts before `suspend.target` finishes, so the journal order described in the reply is not what to look for at this head.

### A docked clamshell suspend still self-wakes and stays awake

`pre` checks only `omarchy-hw-laptop-closed` (`battery-floor:60`), not external monitors, although its comment lists "docked clamshell" as an open-lid case. At expiry `act` stands down when docked (`battery-floor:40`), and logind ignores a docked lid switch by default. A stubbed run confirms the sequence: arm at `pre`, expire, `act` makes no call.

**Impact:** A menu suspend in clamshell mode wakes after 20 minutes and stays awake. This contradicts the "lid-closed, undocked" wording in the manual and setup prompt.

**Suggested change:** Skip arming at `pre` when an external monitor is connected, as `omarchy-system-lid-close` does, or re-suspend from `act` when docked.

**Documentation:** `manual/36-system-sleep.md` says the machine "powers off cleanly" at expiry, but on AC `act` suspends again (`battery-floor:45-47`). The manual line "the decision runs after the suspend job completes" depends on the ordering fix above.

**Optional test improvement:** The early-wake check `grep -Eq $'rtcwake\t-m no -s 1[0-9]{2}'` (`battery-floor-test.sh:193`) is unanchored and also matches `-s 1200`. A mutant that re-arms the full 1200 s in `post` passes all 31 checks, and no case runs a lid-shut `pre` while an earlier deadline is still pending. Exact values with a fixed clock, plus that case, would catch the countdown restart.

**Verified:**
- The PR's test passes on `bbcb542a` (31 checks) and on a clean synthetic merge with the current `quattro` tip. `bin-style`, `manifest-entrypoints` and `omarchy commands --check` pass on both. The full shell suite fails the same 11 files on the merge and on `quattro` alone.
- The transient unit gets `$0` as the full hook path and a default `PATH` that includes `/usr/bin`, so `act` and the bare `omarchy-*` helpers resolve. The deadline file lives in `/run`, so a reboot clears it.
- The earlier review's other Verified points about the hook and setup still hold: the setup logic is unchanged apart from its messages. The earlier mutation result applied to the old test; against the new test, 10 of 15 hook mutants are caught.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of PR head `bbcb542a` against the earlier head `3cb31d17`, and of systemd v262 and util-linux 2.42.4 for sleep-hook, logind, `systemd-run` and `rtcwake` behavior. The PR's test, related repository tests, a synthetic merge with `quattro`, stubbed multi-phase hook scenarios and hook mutants ran in an isolated sandbox. No real suspend, RTC alarm, logind, `systemd-run` or hardware was exercised. Hook timing on real machines was not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
